value_stream.name: Construction Project Material Staging & Phased Delivery

fields.Participants: Trade Sales Mgr, Category Manager, FP&A

workflows.name: Project Material Consumption vs. Estimate Variance Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Material-takeoff auto-computed from the project dimensions; quotation auto-generated from the takeoff × pricing; project-status auto-tracked from milestone completion
Controls: - CTL-462 (ensure controlled execution — Project Material Reconciliation & Analytics (PA-77.3).)
- operational: Trade Sales Manager sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: the project scope expands beyond the original quotation, eroding margin; mitigated by the change-order process and the scope-confirmation sign-off

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
- Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113)
Time Estimate: - Frequency: Per project; quarterly portfolio review
- Absorbed into the Trade Sales Manager role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Trade Sales Manager compares estimated vs. actual: per-item variance, variance % per category, total project variance in PHP; identifies consistent over/under-estimation
Category Manager investigates significant variances: over-estimation (surplus/returns) vs. under-estimation (rush orders); develops improved estimation templates
FP&A incorporates into pricing model: adjusts estimation factors, improves margin prediction, develops project-type benchmarks; presents quarterly to CFO

fields.Participants: Logistics Analyst, Logistics Manager, Trade Sales Manager

Automation Opportunity: - Delivery scheduling auto-optimized from the route/dock/traffic data; real-time tracking auto-pushed to customer and store; POD auto-captured digitally
Controls: - CTL-462 (ensure controlled execution — Project Material Reconciliation & Analytics (PA-77.3).)
- operational: Logistics Analyst sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Delivery-failure risk**: a delivery misses its window (traffic, access, scheduling), disrupting the customer/project; mitigated by the real-time tracking and the rescheduling protocol

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Order management (links to VS-08 / W536 unified order management, VS-60 / W2286 routing)
- Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113 BI platform, W231 QBR dashboard)
Time Estimate: - Absorbed into the Logistics Analyst role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Logistics Analyst tracks project delivery KPIs: on-time rate (≥95%), phase lead time, accuracy, damage rate, emergency frequency; compares vs. standard retail metrics
Analyst identifies patterns: consistently late projects, damage-prone categories, challenging regions; produces recommendations
Trade Sales Manager incorporates into contractor relationship: shares metrics in quarterly reviews, sets delivery expectations for new projects

steps.activity: FP&A Manager compiles portfolio performance: total revenue (target: ~PHP 5B/year, ~8% of total), average margin (25–30%), project mix, revenue pipeline
Manager analyzes margin drivers: project size, category mix, delivery cost, price lock effect, change order impact; identifies improvement opportunities
CFO reviews with VP Merchandising: adjusts pricing strategy, sets margin targets, approves concessions; presents quarterly to CEO

fields.Participants: Finance Analyst, Supply Planning Manager, CFO
fields.Trigger: Quarterly analysis cycle — Project Inventory Carrying Cost

Automation Opportunity: - API-driven real-time sync (catalog, inventory, pricing, orders) eliminating manual data entry; auto-reconciliation of marketplace settlement vs. BuildRight records
Controls: - CTL-462 (ensure controlled execution — Project Material Reconciliation & Analytics (PA-77.3).)
- operational: inventory-count integrity; Operational: Finance Analyst sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: pricing miscalculation (commission, discount, surcharge) erodes net margin below target; mitigated by the margin-floor guard and pre-launch validation
- **Inventory-desync risk**: marketplace inventory sync lags, causing overselling (listing items already sold); mitigated by the real-time ATP sync and the buffer-stock reservation
System Touchpoints: - Inventory/ATP (links to VS-05 / W105 multi-channel allocation, VS-29 / W252 item master)
- Pricing/financials (links to VS-17 / W9 financial close, VS-29 / W289 pricing master)
- Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
Time Estimate: - Absorbed into the Finance Analyst role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Finance Analyst calculates carrying cost: average reserved inventory value (PHP 200M–500M), carrying rate (~15–20% annually), cost per project per month
Analyst identifies high cost projects: long duration, early reservation, slow phase delivery; recommends optimization (reduce lead time, consignment, just-in-phase)
Finance Controller incorporates into pricing: adjusts quotes for carrying cost; Trade Sales Manager uses to negotiate better payment terms

fields.Participants: Supply Planning Mgr, Procurement, Trade Sales Manager, VP Supply Chain

workflows.name: Project Supply Chain Risk & Resilience Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Credit-score auto-computed from the financial-data feed; credit-limit auto-suggested from the scoring model; collection-aging auto-tracked with escalation
Controls: - CTL-462 (ensure controlled execution — Project Material Reconciliation & Analytics (PA-77.3).)
- CTL-462 (credit-authorization — links to VS-16 / W24); Operational: Supply Planning Manager sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Credit-default risk**: a trade account defaults on extended credit, creating a bad-debt write-off; mitigated by the credit-scoring model and the credit-limit monitoring

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/risk (links to VS-22 / regulatory, VS-86 / AML, VS-91 / privacy)
- Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113 BI platform, W231 QBR dashboard)
Time Estimate: - Absorbed into the Supply Planning Manager role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Supply Planning Manager assesses risks: vendor concentration, import dependency, DC capacity, weather, geopolitical; per project
Manager develops mitigation: alternative vendors, safety stock, flexible scheduling, strategic pre-positioning; quantifies risk exposure in PHP per project
VP Supply Chain reviews risk portfolio: total exposure, concentration, insurance adequacy, contingency budget; approves mitigation investments
